name: Pakistan

latest_census.notes: 7th Population and Housing Census 2023 ('first-ever digital census'). Religion and mother tongue are asked; there is no ethnicity question (mother tongue is the local proxy). Both are published subnationally: Table 9 'Population by sex, religion and rural/urban' and Table 11 'Population by mother tongue, sex and rural/urban' are issued per province by province/division/district/tehsil as PDFs on pbs.gov.pk/digital-census/detailed-results; District Census Reports 2023 carry Table 3.6 (% by religion) and 3.7 (% by mother tongue); the National Census Report 2023 has Tables 4.13/4.14 for 2017 vs 2023. AJK and Gilgit-Baltistan were enumerated (10 census districts each per PBS 'Number of Census Areas 2023'), but geo-ref.net notes their datasets were 'not complete ... partially included only as 2017 data'. The repo already reads Table 9 (religion, 114/126 districts) and takes mother tongue from the 2017 USCB workbook.

summary: Pakistan's 2023 census counts religion (Table 9) and mother tongue (Table 11) and publishes both by province, division, district and tehsil as PDFs on pbs.gov.pk/digital-census/detailed-results; the repo already parses Table 9 for 114 of 126 districts but still takes language from the 2017 USCB workbook. The 2023 Table 11 PDFs are the direct upgrade, and two keyless machine-readable copies now exist to check against: the CRAN package PakPC2023 (PakPC2023PakDist with TABLE_09 and TABLE_11 by district, dated July 2025) and a GitHub XLSX conversion of the District Wise PDFs. The District Census Report 2023 for Islamabad carries religion and mother-tongue percentages (Tables 3.6/3.7), a third PBS path that fills the ICT gap the adapter recorded. AJK and Gilgit-Baltistan were enumerated (10 census districts each) but no religion or mother-tongue table for them surfaced and one source says their 2023 data was incomplete. Ethnicity is not asked. The three admin2 Wikipedia sample checks were not run because the session's search budget ran out.
